validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to every fetch attempt (confirmed directly with curl -A Mozilla, not just the harvester), so there is no wiki-cited source to re-verify -- this row's only support is whatever GEM itself asserts. I then searched the open web (DuckDuckGo lite/html, Bing, Google, Brave, Mojeek, Ecosia -- WebSearch tool budget was exhausted for the session so I used WebFetch against each engine's results page directly) for the exact pipeline name 'Wah-Nowshera Gas Pipeline I' / 'Wah-Nowshera' + gas pipeline. Every engine's TOP (and only) hits for the exact phrase are GEM's own two wiki pages (Wah-Nowshera Gas Pipeline I and II) -- no independent outlet, SNGPL document, OGRA report, or Wikipedia page uses this name or cites a 10-inch/50.41 km segment between Wah and Nowshera. That is a genuine existence/specificity red flag consistent with the scope note that this whole 2023-07 batch looks like a bulk load. HOWEVER, the surrounding context is NOT empty: (1) two live SNGPL tender notices on sngpl.com.pk (SNGPL's own site, HTTP 200, read directly -- 'WAHPLO0112021.pdf' dated 2021-11-04 and 'WAHPLO033202425.pdf' dated 2025-04-21) confirm SNGPL operates a real administrative region called 'Wah Transmission' headquartered at Gadwal Link Road, Lala Rukh, Wah Cantt, and that this region's jurisdiction extends into Nowshera district, KP (one tender is for civil works on a 24-inch Kohat-Ismailkot pipeline at 'Tehsil Pabbi, District Nowshera'; the region's Executive Engineer contact code is literally 'C10 Nowshera'); (2) Wikipedia's Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited article states 'The main transmission regions of SNGPL are Faisalabad, Lahore, Multan, and Wah' -- i.e. Wah is independently confirmed as one of only four major SNGPL transmission hubs, and the same article notes SNGPL's historical takeover of a 'Dhulian-Rawalpindi-Wah system,' so Wah is a genuine, long-standing transmission junction, not an invented place; (3) the roster shows Nowshera is a real multi-line SNGPL hub too (P4176 Kohat-Nowshera, P4179 Nowshera-Mardan-Takht Bhai-Sakhakot both terminate/originate at Nowshera). So a Wah<->Nowshera trunk corridor fitting into this real network is entirely plausible, and the specific decimal-precision lengths in this batch (50.41 km, 52.6 km, not round numbers) look like genuine mile-point survey data of the kind SNGPL's own tenders reference (e.g. 'MP41.11', 'MP41.43') rather than fabricated placeholders. Net assessment: the CORRIDOR and OWNER are well supported by independent sources; the SPECIFIC named/sized segment 'Wah-Nowshera Gas Pipeline I' (50.41 km, 10in) is not independently confirmed anywhere I could reach. This is a real, bounded existence concern -- not 'this is almost certainly a phantom' but 'this specific row cannot be independently corroborated beyond GEM's own page, only the broader network it would belong to.'

Tier held at medium rather than high because both sources, while independent of each other and of GEM, corroborate the jurisdiction rather than the named asset.

validity.researcher_notes: Classification check: Fuel=Gas is trivially consistent (this is a natural-gas trunk line, not disputed). PipelineType=transmission is consistent with SNGPL's own usage -- the 'Wah Transmission' region's tenders describe pipelines from 8in up to 24in+ diameter all under the 'Transmission' banner (e.g. the 24in Kohat-Ismailkot line above), and the roster's Punjab/KP block contains many 8-16in lines all similarly labeled transmission, so a 10in line under the same regional office is not an outlier or a gathering/feeder line mislabeled as transmission. Duplicate check against the 63-row roster: the only close match is P4173 'Wah-Nowshera Gas Pipeline II' (52.6 km, 16in) -- same endpoints, different diameter and slightly different length. This fits the roster's repeated main-line + parallel-loop pattern seen elsewhere with identical naming convention (e.g. P4161/P4162 Dandot-Gali Jagir-Wah I/II, P4106/P4107 Sidhnai-Faisalabad I/II, P4108/P4140 Sahiwal-Lahore I/II, P4135/P4136 Faisalabad-Shahdara I/II) -- two physically distinct pipes of different diameter laid at different times along the same corridor, not a double-count of one pipe. Concluding this is NOT a duplicate, subject to the same existence caveat noted above (i.e. if the corridor itself turns out to be a single mis-split entity, both P4170 and P4173 would need re-examination together, but on the current evidence they read as a legitimate main+loop pair).
